answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to prove a unique, costly history before it can earn rewards. A newcomer must complete verified work over time, not merely register, so a flood of fresh identities cannot outvote established contributors. Like a comet that leaves a visible trail, every action is logged; a lantern of auditability lets peers check that trail, and a prism view that splits one operator's activity across many names reveals shared funding, timing, or behavior. Rewards then follow proven contribution, not headcount, so creating extra identities buys no extra influence.
